title: Undo for reversible actions
summary: Prefer immediate completion plus a contextual undo for low-to-medium-risk reversible actions instead of interrupting every action with confirmation.
problem: Excess confirmation dialogs slow routine work and train users to confirm without reading.
use_when: The action can be reliably reversed without hidden side effects
The user benefits from fast repetitive work
avoid_when: The action is irreversible, legally consequential, or reversal cannot restore the prior state
rationale: Undo keeps momentum while still protecting against slips.
Confirmation is more valuable when consequence is genuinely hard to recover.

use_if: The action can be reliably reversed without hidden side effects
The user benefits from fast repetitive work
prefer_alternatives_if: The operation cannot be fully or reliably reversed

requirements: Make undo reachable by keyboard and assistive technology.
Do not rely on a disappearing visual message as the only recovery path for significant actions.
Only promise undo when restoration is complete and reliable.
Keep recovery visible long enough for the task context.
Explain when reversal has downstream consequences.
